decision.evidence: Confirmed refuter: mesh family index alone does not bound cell diameters. Defined h=max({0} union {diam K}) to preserve the empty mesh with h=0 and guarantee h_K<=h for every cell. Read all current mesh/reference-element/polynomial-space/local-estimate and measure supplier statements. For d=2,3, p=2, ell=r=2, m=1, k=1 the interpolation theorem applies with expressly assumed bounded nodal DOFs, without its optional AC-based point-evaluation result. Unisolvence identifies global restrictions with local interpolants; traces match at face vertices and membership in V is assumed. Finite facets are null by affine graph content, Jordan/Lebesgue equality and completeness; coordinate permutations merely permute covering boxes and preserve content, allowing any nonzero normal coordinate. Null skeleton and nonnegative-integral measure property give exact seminorm decomposition, including empty sum. Sum local squared errors, h_K<=h and the stipulated C_V bound, then substitute I_hu into first Strang. All defects remain explicit; empty mesh is zero-function case. No consumer items reference this corollary.

target.evidence: The Statement uses h in the error bound and calls the approximation contribution O(h), but does not define h or relate it to the cell diameters. The cited mesh Definition defines h_K := diam(K) and shape regularity of a family indexed by h, but does not state h = max_K h_K or h_K ≤ h. The proof uses h_K ≤ h in step 2.1. Moreover, def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces says an empty mesh is allowed (if T = empty, then Ω = empty), so a maximum cell diameter cannot supply h in every admitted case. As written, the rate is not licensed for a determined mesh size.
